What most designers think of as ‘UI Animation’ is in fact the execution of a higher modality of design: the temporal behavior of interface objects during realtime and non-realtime events.

  

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- State / Act
- Realtime vs Non Realtime Interactions
- Realtime interactions can be thought of direct manipulation

  

Motion supports usability in four ways:

- Expectation

- How the object is perceived and how it behaves

- Continuity

- Flow and consistency
- Intra continuity and inter continuity

- Narrative

- Linear progression of events that results in the framework

- Relationship

Principles

Techniques  - style/ executions

Properties - parameters

Values - numeric properties

  

![](data:image/png;base64,)

  

## Principle 1: Easing

Slow in, slow out. Everything that moves should ease.
  
## Principle 2: Offset & Delay

Defines relationships and hierarchies
Separates objects

  

## Principle 3: Parenting

Spatial and temporal hierarchical relationships
Object properties:

- Scale
- Opacity
- Position
- Rotation
- Shape
- Colour
- Value
- etc

Works best in real time.
Direct, delayed and inverse parenting

![](data:image/png;base64,)

  
  

## Principle 4: Transformation

Creates a continuous state of narrative flow when object utility changes
Seamlessly transition the user through different UX states
Chunking

  

## Principle 5: Value Change

Connect the user to the reality behind the data, the concept of agency and to the dynamic nature of the values themselves.
  
## Principle 6: Masking

The act of masking can be thought of as a relationship between the shape of the object and its utility. 
As an act.

## Principle 7: Overlay

Using flatland to communicate location dependent objects that exist behind or in front of others

## Principle 8: Cloning

Continuity, relationship and narrative when new objects originate and depart.
Directing of attention.

  

## Principle 9: Obscuration

Allows users to spatially orient themselves in relationship to objects or scenes not in the primary visual hierarchy.
Temporal phenomena.
The moments between the moments.

  

## Principle 10: Parallax

Creates spatial hierarchy  in visual flatland when users scroll.
Different objects moving at different rates.
Focus on primary actions and content while maintaining design integrity.

  

## Principle 11: Dimensionality

Provides a spatial narrative framework when new objects originate and depart.
Sense of location.
Origami Dimensionality - folding/hinged objects
Floating Dimensionality - cards etc
Object Dimensionality - true depth and form

  

## Principle 12: Dolly & Zoom

Preserves continuity and spatial narrative when navigating interface objects and spaces.
Movement of objects relative to camera
Dolly - moving the camera towards or away from subject
Zoom - object itself is scaling - shows additional objects inside
